question: Which ISRO mission, successfully completed in January 2025, demonstrated autonomous docking between two satellites?
solution:
The correct answer is __**SPADEX**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **SPADEX** (Space Docking Experiment) is an ambitious project of the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** aimed at demonstrating autonomous docking capabilities between two satellites.
 
• The experiment is crucial for future missions involving **space stations**, in-orbit servicing, and refueling spacecraft.
 
• SPADEX successfully completed its autonomous docking demonstration in **January 2025**, marking a significant milestone in India's space technology development.
 
• The docking process involves precise navigation, control systems, and sensors, enabling two spacecraft to connect in orbit without human intervention.
 
• This mission establishes India’s capability to conduct complex space operations and supports advancements in satellite repair and maintenance technologies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SPADEX (Space Docking Experiment):**

 
 
• SPADEX is developed by **ISRO** to test autonomous docking technologies, a critical feature for future space stations and spacecraft servicing missions.
 
• This technology enables satellites to dock together in orbit for activities such as refueling, repairing, or even assembling larger structures.
 
• The experiment includes two spacecraft, one acting as a target and the other as a chaser, showcasing precision navigation and control.
 
• The success of SPADEX demonstrates India’s growing expertise in **satellite and orbital technologies**.
 
 
 
• **Gaganyaan Mission:**
 
 
• The **Gaganyaan Mission** is India’s first human spaceflight program, aiming to send astronauts into low Earth orbit.
 
• It is expected to launch by **2024**, focusing on crew safety, space habitation, and life-support systems.
 
• While advanced technology is involved, Gaganyaan is not directly related to autonomous docking.
 
 
 
• **Aditya-L1:**
 
 
• Aditya-L1 is India's first solar mission, launched to study the Sun’s corona, chromosphere, and solar wind.
 
• It focuses on scientific exploration rather than demonstrating autonomous docking.
 
 
 
• **Chandrayaan-3:**
 
 
• Chandrayaan-3 is a lunar exploration mission by ISRO, which successfully soft-landed on the Moon.
 
• This mission is unrelated to autonomous docking and focuses primarily on lunar surface studies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Autonomous Docking:**

 
 
• Autonomous docking is a complex space operation requiring advanced sensors, navigation systems, and control algorithms.
 
• It is essential for future space missions involving multi-satellite systems, space stations, and reusable spacecraft.
 
 
 
• **ISRO's Achievements:**
 
 
• ISRO continues to innovate with missions like **SPADEX, Chandrayaan, and Gaganyaan**, expanding India’s space capabilities.
 
• The success of SPADEX highlights India’s capability to develop cutting-edge space technologies for international collaboration and exploration.
